title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrations, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures, checklists, and templates Customer Success (CS) and Support use when onboarding enterprise customers to Redwood Inference. It covers integration validation, escalation paths and SLAs, known issues and workarounds, health-check cadence, and Quarter‑back Review (QBR) materials.

Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments, and enterprise-heavy usage on Hosted API). This document is intended for CSMs, Technical Account Managers (TAMs), Support Engineers, SREs, and Partner Integrators.

Audience: Customer Success, Support, SRE, Eng (when on-call for escalations), and Solutions Engineering.

Summary: Follow the phases below for predictable, low-risk onboarding: Kickoff -> Integration & Validation -> Performance & Cost Tuning -> Production Cutover -> Ongoing Health & QBRs. Use the escalation section for incidents; use the integration checklist and known-issues table during validation.

--

1) Onboarding phases (high level)

1. Kickoff (owner: CSM)
   - Deliverables: project plan, success criteria, technical contacts, access matrix, NDA/KV exchange.
   - Timeline: typical 2–6 weeks depending on scope.
   - Key artifacts: onboarding plan (shared Google sheet), security questionnaire, sample prompt corpus.

2. Integration & Validation (owner: Solutions Engineering / TAM)
   - Verifications: API key creation, network connectivity (VPC peering or IP allowlist), model pinning, webhook/event ingestion, logging/observability hooks.
   - Run integration tests: basic generation, streaming, embeddings, and tool/function calls.
   - Acceptance criteria: all checklists green; sample prompts produce expected output quality baseline.

3. Performance & Cost Tuning (owner: Solutions Engineering / Eng-Platform)
   - Tasks: configure batching, caching, quantization recommendation, route policies (fallback model tiers), and autoscaling rules for Dedicated.
   - Metrics to validate: p50/p95/p99 latency, average tokens/request, tokens/sec throughput, unit cost per 1k tokens.

4. Production cutover (owner: CSM + Customer ops)
   - Steps: final sync, feature flags rollout, canary vs full cutover, traffic ramp schedule (suggested: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 72–168 hours depending on risk).
   - Rollback criteria: increased error rate > 1% above baseline for 30 minutes OR sustained p99 latency > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.

5. Ongoing health, QBRs, and runbook handover (owner: CSM / TAM)
   - Cadence: weekly health-checks for first 8 weeks, monthly thereafter; QBRs on a 90‑day cadence for Enterprise.
   - Deliverables: health dashboard share, cost optimization recommendations, model quality regressions report.

--

2) Integration checklist (must pass before cutover)

Mandatory items:
- API access
  - Customer has a service account and API key scoped to intended resources and environment.
  - Validate with a smoke test:
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Hello world"}'
  - Expected response: 200 + coherent text.

- Network & Security
  - For Private/Dedicated: confirm VPC peering, route tables, and security groups. Validate egress rules for telemetry endpoints.
  - Confirm KMS/HSM integration for encryption-at-rest (if required).

- Model configuration
  - Model pinning YAML example (customer-config):
    model_pin: rwd-small-1@v2026-02-15
    fallback_model: rwd-small-1-quantized@v2026-02-15
  - Validate tokenization and encoding (UTF-8).

- Webhooks & Eventing
  - Confirm webhook endpoints, signing secret exchange, and retry/backoff behavior.
  - Sample webhook payload included in templates library.

- Observability & Logging
  - Ensure ingestion to customer-owned SIEM (if configured) and Redwood Console access.
  - Instrumentation keys and trace hooks provided; validate a trace across request -> runtime -> response.

- Data & Privacy
  - Confirm data residency and retention policy settings.
  - Validate audit logging and delete/retention APIs if customer requires.

Optional but recommended:
- Autoscaling policy review for Dedicated pools (min/max GPUs, buffer capacity).
- KV/prefix caching policy tuned for prompt patterns.
- Batching window configuration for interactive vs batch workloads.

Acceptance checklist must be added to the onboarding ticket and signed off by Customer and CSM.

--

3) Escalation playbook (summary)

Severity definitions and SLAs:
- Sev1 (Service Down / Critical Production Impact)
  - Definition: Entire customer production traffic fails, or platform unavailable for > 50% of requests.
  - Initial response SLA: 15 minutes.
  - Target resolution: 4 hours (depends on root cause and mitigations).

- Sev2 (Major Degradation)
  - Definition: Significant feature loss (streaming broken, model responses corrupted) or high error rates (>5% of traffic).
  - Initial response SLA: 1 hour.
  - Target resolution: 24 hours.

- Sev3 (Partial Degradation / Non-critical)
  - Definition: Intermittent errors, single-route regressions, or degraded but usable performance.
  - Initial response SLA: 4 business hours.
  - Target resolution: 3–7 business days.

- Sev4 (Minor / Request)
  - Definition: Feature requests, minor cosmetic issues, or questions.
  - Response SLA: 3 business days.

Escalation chain (required information must be present in ticket):
1. Customer reports incident -> CSM creates/supports Support ticket with triage data.
2. Support L1 triage: collect reproduction steps, request id(s), model name/version, timestamps, and raw request/response samples (redact PII).
3. If L1 cannot resolve within SLA, escalate to Support L2 and tag on-call SRE.
4. Support L2 runs deeper diagnostics (profiling, traces, runtime logs) and engages Eng-serving-runtime and SRE as needed.
5. If root cause indicates infra or runtime bug, open an internal incident and notify Eng on-call; for customer-impacting changes require mitigation plan and customer communication cadence (hourly for Sev1, every 4 hours for Sev2).

Required ticket fields (Support system template):
- Customer name, environment (prod/staging), endpoint/route, request ids, start/end timestamp, severity, observed behavior, reproduction steps, screenshots/log snippets, impacted percentage of traffic, workaround (if any), CSM contact.

Communication guidelines:
- For Sev1: triage note within 15 minutes, public status update to customer every 60 minutes until mitigated.
- For Sev2: initial triage within 1 hour, updates every 4 hours.
- Share postmortem within 72 hours (interim) and full RCA within 7 calendar days for Sev1.

Escalation contacts (roles)
- Primary CSM: listed per account (CS system)
- Support L2 lead: support-l2@redwood.example.com
- SRE on-call: see eng-sre/oncall schedule (link)
- Eng-serving-runtime on-call: see runtime oncall roster (link)

--

4) Known issues & workarounds (operational digest)

| Issue ID | Symptom | Workaround | Owner | Status |
|----------|---------|------------|-------|--------|
| KI-2026-001 | Streaming truncation for long-lived connections on older gateways | Force chunked mode: set streaming_mode=chunked; ensure gateway upgrade; temporary: retry with smaller max_tokens | eng-platform | monitoring |
| KI-2026-010 | Elevated 500 errors for embedding route under high concurrency | Apply burst capacity: route to dedicated embedding pool; increase concurrency limit per client; enable caching layer | eng-serving-runtime | investigating |
| KI-2025-087 | Tokenization mismatch for emojis in customer corpus | Normalize inputs to NFC form before send; apply pre-tokenizer pipeline step in SDK | docs + eng-developer-experience | resolved |

How to contribute a known issue: create a ticket in Support with label "known-issue" and add reproduction steps + logs. Owners will triage weekly and update status in the issue table.

--

5) Health checks and QBR materials

Health dashboard (shareable): recommended widgets
- Availability (7d/30d) — target: 99.9% for Dedicated; Hosted enterprise target 99.5%.
- Latency distribution: p50/p95/p99 for generation and embedding routes. Target p99: <= 2s for interactive workloads on Dedicated; hosted targets are model-dependent and should be documented in catalog.
- Error rate: 5xx and 4xx rates per route. Target: <0.5% sustained.
- Cost metrics: tokens per request, avg cost per 1k tokens, trend of cost by model.
- Model quality indicators: % of prompts failing evaluation tests, fuzz/regression alerts.

Weekly health-check template (first 8 weeks)
1. Summary: traffic, new integrations, outstanding high-sev tickets.
2. Key metrics: availability, p99 latency, error rate, cost delta.
3. Actions: optimization recommendations and owner assignments.
4. Blockers: network, security, data residency issues.

QBR template (90-day cadence)
- Executive summary (1 page)
- Adoption and usage: active users, requests/day, growth rate
- Performance & reliability: SLO compliance, major incidents, mean time to resolve
- Cost & optimization: spend vs forecast, opportunities (quantization, routing)
- Roadmap alignment & requests: model onboarding, feature requests
- Action plan and owners (next 90 days)

Deliverables: QBR slide deck, export of dashboard metrics, change-log since last QBR, and three prioritized success actions.

--

6) Runbook & postmortem requirements

- For any Sev1 incident, assign a postmortem author within 24 hours. Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, impact, mitigation, and a 90-day action plan with owners.
- Track action item completion in the onboarding ticket or customer Success plan.

--

7) Templates and quick references (links)
- Onboarding plan template: confluence/customer-success-and-support/templates/onboarding-plan
- Support ticket template: support/templates/enterprise-incident
- QBR slide template: confluence/customer-success-and-support/templates/qbr-deck
- Known issues board: support/known-issues

--

Appendix: Troubleshooting quick commands
- Verify API key: curl -I -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health
- Collect request trace: include header X-Trace-Request: true in reproducer; attach trace id to ticket.

Ownership & contact matrix
- Customer Success lead: primary point for business and go/no-go.
- Solutions Engineering: technical integration and performance tuning.
- Support (L1/L2): incident triage and remediation.
- SRE / Eng-serving-runtime: infrastructure and runtime escalations.

This playbook should be reviewed at least quarterly or after any major platform change that impacts customer-facing behavior (new streaming protocol, major kernel upgrade, or changes to batch/caching semantics). For feedback or updates, contact the document owner (Maya Chen) or use the reviewers list.
